FROM WORKING PROTOTYPE TO REAL SERVICE

Your Singapore launch playbook.

The website is a working, static beta. Use it to test the experience now, then connect live services in stages. Adding an API key to a static page will not activate integrations: those features require backend implementation and, in some cases, partner approval.

What works today

12 curated places; keyword-based intent matching; neighborhood, time and budget filters; place details; walking/transit links; add, remove and reorder day stops; local saving; text export; dated hotel search handoff; external Klook and Grab links. No account or API key is needed.

01 / Run the website on your computer

  1. Install a supported Node.js LTS release, version 22 or later.
  2. Open a terminal in the wandersea project folder.
  3. Run the checks and start the local server:
npm run check
npm test
npm run dev

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. There are no npm dependencies to install. Use Ctrl+C to stop the server.

Edit dist/index.html for the page, dist/styles.css for the design, dist/engine.js for catalog/matching and dist/app.js for interactions. This is plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, not the unprovided Next.js ZIP described in the earlier reference.

02 / Add live places, maps and routes

  1. Create a project in Google Cloud Console and attach billing.
  2. Enable Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New) and Routes API. Enable Maps Grounding Lite separately if choosing it for AI grounding.
  3. Create a browser key. Restrict it to your development and production website origins and only the required browser APIs. Use a separate production key.
  4. Create separate server credentials for backend calls. Use appropriate API restrictions and supported IP/OAuth restrictions. If serverless outbound IPs change, configure supported authentication or stable egress.
  5. Implement a protected backend for Places/Routes calls, with validation, quotas and request limits. Never put private keys into the static files.
  6. Replace the outbound-only map experience with an embedded map and real place selection. Replace the 20-minute transfer placeholders with route estimates.
  7. Apply attribution and permitted caching/storage rules. Configure billing alerts plus quotas; alerts alone do not stop charges.

Google setup · Key security · Places policies

03 / Connect booking providers

Klook activities

  1. Prepare your demo URL, business/project details, contact email and privacy/terms pages.
  2. Apply to the Affiliate Program for tracked links. For deeper distribution, use the partner enquiry and select distributor.
  3. Ask explicitly for Singapore product data, prices, availability, permitted AI use, mobile tracking, sandbox and whether checkout can be embedded.
  4. Replace ordinary search links with approved product links when accepted. API access is separate; implement only against the documentation issued for your distribution agreement.

The public merchant API describes supply-side integration. It does not establish that your app has permission to resell Klook inventory.

Hotels

  1. Start with official hotel links or provider search handoffs. The current beta passes a neighborhood and selected dates to Booking.com; it does not search room inventory.
  2. Apply for Booking.com Managed Affiliate / Demand access, or evaluate Expedia Rapid.
  3. Once approved, implement server-side search with check-in/out, rooms, adults, child ages, taxes/fees and cancellation policies. Match exact supplier property IDs.
  4. Use approved redirect checkout first. Embedded booking also needs price rechecks, duplicate prevention, status recovery, support, cancellations and refunds.

For a direct hotel partnership, contact its sales/e-commerce team. Begin with a tracked link to its booking engine; inventory integration requires its chosen system and a commercial agreement. A Google hotel listing does not provide room availability.

Grab rides

Keep the current external handoff until Grab confirms a supported Singapore ride integration. Request current deep-link documentation and test installed/not-installed behavior. Do not assume GrabPay or delivery access includes consumer ride booking. A click is not a booked ride, fare or pickup estimate.

04 / Connect AI, weather and accounts

Intent-aware AI

  1. Create an API project/key and billing on OpenAI Platform. Keep the key on the server.
  2. Implement the Responses API with structured intent extraction: location, date, party, budget scope, time, interests and hard constraints.
  3. Define bounded backend tools for permitted catalog search, routes, weather and supplier inventory. Use independently owned/licensed data or a compatible Google grounding configuration; review terms and retention before sending Google content to a model.
  4. Calculate itinerary timing and cost in code. Have the model explain verified candidates; never invent current rates, hours or bookings.
  5. Validate outputs and approved URLs. Retain user approval for booking, payment or cancellation actions. Set per-request tool, token and time limits.

Weather

Use the NEA two-hour forecast on data.gov.sg. Sign in, request a developer/production key if needed, copy the selected dataset's current API specification and match the forecast area. Show issue time, validity and service failures.

Accounts and saved trips

Create a Supabase project. Add trip/member/item tables, Auth, scoped sharing and row-level policies. Test with two users. Keep secret/service-role keys server-side. The current browser-local plan should migrate only after the user agrees.

Keep provider-specific secrets in your host's environment settings. The included .env.example is a naming template, not a live integration. For Sites-hosted server features, migrate with the supported server starter and configure runtime secrets; for a Next.js/Supabase stack, build and deploy the backend separately. The full requirements document describes the application endpoints and data entities.

05 / Publish and prepare for partners

  1. The Sites preview is private by default. A public partner-facing demo needs an intentional access change or deployment to a public host.
  2. For independent static hosting, upload the contents of dist/ to a static host, or use a Git-based deployment with no build command and output directory dist. Do not upload private credentials.
  3. Connect your chosen domain and HTTPS. Update the production origin in Google key restrictions and Auth redirects when those services are added.
  4. Replace prototype policy text with your actual business/operator identity, contact, privacy and support information. Confirm media rights and provider terms.
  5. Use the live demo for Klook and hotel applications. State the product is prelaunch and describe traffic honestly.
  6. Before commercial booking, assess STB travel-agent/platform requirements for your exact service flow. Document the provider responsible for payments, confirmations and refunds.

The current site has no contact form, waitlist collection, analytics or email backend. Add those only with the required data handling and consent processes.

06 / Test before making promises

  • Rainy/indoor requests exclude outdoor and covered-only hawker stops.
  • No matches produce an honest empty state rather than ignored constraints.
  • Plans survive refresh, reorder correctly, export and can be deleted.
  • Time and budget overruns are visible. Test actual routes after adding routing.
  • Hotel check-out follows check-in; guests and final rates are confirmed with the provider.
  • External links work on iOS, Android and desktop. Missing apps have fallbacks.
  • No private API key is present in downloaded JavaScript or logs.
  • Live features have failure/stale-data states; cross-user access is blocked.
  • Bookings remain pending/unknown until the supplier confirms them.

Proposed order: test this beta with 5–10 visitors → add real routing and data → improve AI matching → integrate one approved booking partner → expand only after useful repeat usage.
